title: The Science of Pipe Slope and Drainage
description: Gravity is the primary force moving wastewater through a building's drainage network, making correct pipe slope essential for long-term system health. If a horizontal pipe is pitched too steeply, the liquid wastewater rushes past solid waste, leaving the solids behind to accumulate and form clogs. Conversely, if the slope is too flat, water velocity drops below the threshold required to suspend and transport debris. Achieving reliable drainage requires balancing horizontal fall according to local plumbing standards and pipe diameters. Proper maintenance and installation practices ensure waste moves consistently to the main sewer without premature blockages.
